title: The same with numeric positions
summary: Command a two-axis assembler with numeric setpoints in centimetres and a position tolerance instead of limit switches.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Send an axis to a named position with a setpoint and read its position back.
Decide that a move is done when the position is within a tolerance of the setpoint, not when it is equal to it.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Assembler.st, name the positions as constants (lid belt x 0, base belt x 100, down y 0, safe height y 30, tolerance 0.2 cm), write XSet and YSet in one state per move, and move on when XAt or YAt says the pad is within the tolerance.
stages.checkpoint: Each move is one setpoint and one comparison; the pad never crosses the belts below the safe height.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the numbers for one lid: y goes to 30, x to 0, y to 0, the vacuum grips, y to 30, x to 100, y to 0, the vacuum lets go, y to 30 and x back to 0.
stages.checkpoint: XPos and YPos reach each setpoint within 0.2 cm before the next state starts; the vacuum is on only between the grip and the release.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter commands no position, so the pad stays where it is; send it to the lid, grip, carry the lid to the base and release it, three times, and light Green after the third.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named two-axis-assembly-numeric and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch XPos and YPos in the trace come to each setpoint, and the pad in the 3D view cross the belts only at the safe height.
stages.checkpoint: A lid is set on each base, nothing is dropped, and Green is on at the end.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A position is a measurement, so a comparison with a tolerance is the correct test; an exact equality of two REAL values can fail forever. The scenario proves that an assembly was made and delivered, that nothing was dropped and that Green is on at the end. It cannot read a position value, so it does not check your tolerance or your setpoints.
stages.checkpoint: It does not establish physical gripper timing, axis speed, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: Write XAt := ABS(XPos - XSet) < Tol; and the same for Y, and let each state change only when its At flag is TRUE.
Raise to the safe height first, then move in X, then lower; set the setpoint when you enter the state, not on every scan of a state that waits.

faultCases: The starter commands no position, so the pad stays where it is; send it to the lid, grip, carry the lid to the base and release it, three times, and light Green after the third.
